summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for post-procedural observation after undergoing transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) of a 5.2 cm liver tumor in segment VI/VII and smaller lesions in segment VIII. The procedure was uncomplicated, with successful delivery of doxorubicin-lipiodol and no non-target embolization. He remained stable throughout admission, with no significant pain, nausea, or complications. Post-procedure CT confirmed good lipiodol uptake in the target lesions and no ectopic distribution. Liver enzymes rose modestly as expected. He was discharged home the following day with instructions to monitor for post-embolization symptoms, complete outpatient lab testing, and follow up with oncology and hepatology. All home medications, including nadolol, diuretics, and omeprazole, were continued.
